instruction: When is the best time to plant maize in Nigeria?
response:
There are two windows: an early-season crop planted around April-June with the first rains, and a late-season crop around October-November where a second rainy period allows it. Maize is grown across Nigeria, from the northern Guinea savanna to the south.

To get the most from the season: Plant improved/hybrid seed at 75 cm x 25 cm (one plant per stand, ~53,000 plants/ha). On most soils apply about 4 bags/ha (200 kg/ha) of NPK 15:15:15 at planting and top-dress with ~2 bags/ha (100 kg/ha) of urea at 5-6 weeks; adjust to your soil-test result.

instruction: How long does maize take to be ready for harvest after planting?
response: Maize takes about 3.5 months (~15 weeks) from planting to harvest in Nigerian conditions. Plan your planting date so this maturity period falls within the rains and the crop matures before the dry season sets in.

instruction: What yield can I expect from maize on my farm in Nigeria?
response: Typical maize yields in Nigeria run about 1.1-3.0 t/ha (typically around 2.1 t/ha). Where farmers fall short it is usually seed quality, spacing or soil fertility. To push toward the upper end: Plant improved/hybrid seed at 75 cm x 25 cm (one plant per stand, ~53,000 plants/ha). On most soils apply about 4 bags/ha (200 kg/ha) of NPK 15:15:15 at planting and top-dress with ~2 bags/ha (100 kg/ha) of urea at 5-6 weeks; adjust to your soil-test result.

instruction: When is the best time to plant rice in Nigeria?
response:
Plant rice around May-July, once the rains have settled in. Rice is grown in the fadama and inland valleys of the north and middle belt.

To get the most from the season: Use a certified variety such as FARO 44 or FARO 66, transplant 21-day seedlings at 20 cm x 20 cm, and split nitrogen: ~3 bags/ha NPK at transplanting plus urea top-dressings at tillering and panicle initiation. Keep 3-5 cm of standing water during tillering.

response:

instruction: When is the best time to plant millet in Nigeria?
response:
Plant millet around May-July, once the rains have settled in. Millet is grown in the driest north (Sudan and Sahel savanna).

To get the most from the season: Sow on ridges at 75 cm x 30 cm as the rains stabilise. Millet needs little fertiliser -- ~1-2 bags/ha NPK plus a light urea top-dressing is enough on poor sandy soils. Thin to 2-3 plants per stand.

instruction: When is the best time to plant groundnut in Nigeria?
response:
Plant groundnut around May-July, once the rains have settled in. Groundnut is grown in the northern and middle-belt savanna.

To get the most from the season: Space at 45-75 cm x 10-15 cm. As a legume it fixes its own nitrogen, so skip urea; apply single super phosphate (SSP) at ~1-2 bags/ha and gypsum (~200-400 kg/ha) at flowering for good pod filling.

instruction: When is the best time to plant soybean in Nigeria?
response:
Soybean is flexible on timing and is planted across much of the year, but establish it at the onset of the rains (around March-April in the south) so it grows into the wet season. Soybean is grown in the middle belt and northern Guinea savanna.

To get the most from the season: Inoculate the seed with rhizobium, drill at 45-75 cm rows, and skip nitrogen; apply SSP at ~1-2 bags/ha. Use a promiscuous-nodulating variety (e.g. TGx lines) if inoculant is unavailable.

instruction: When is the best time to plant cassava in Nigeria?
response:

instruction: When is the best time to plant yam in Nigeria?
response:
Plant yam around February-April, once the rains have settled in. Yam is grown in the yam belt of the middle belt and south-east.

To get the most from the season: Plant setts (~200-300 g) on mounds or ridges at ~1 m spacing and stake the vines. Treat setts against rot before planting and apply ~2-3 bags/ha NPK; avoid heavy nitrogen, which favours vine over tuber.
